# Clarify Requirements

Resolve only ambiguity that can materially change the result. Do not implement unless the user separately authorizes implementation.

## Build the decision map

1. Restate the requested outcome in one sentence.
2. Inspect user-authorized context for answers that are safely discoverable. Do not ask the user to repeat facts already established.
3. List plausible interpretations privately. Treat a choice as material when it changes observable behavior, scope, safety, compatibility, cost, reversibility, or acceptance.
4. Track each material decision as `confirmed`, `inferred`, or `open`, with its evidence. Never silently default an open material decision.

Consider these lenses only when relevant: actors and permissions; inputs and outputs; happy path; edge, failure, and misuse behavior; data lifecycle; compatibility; operational constraints; rollout and rollback; acceptance evidence.

## Interview

Ask the highest-leverage open question first. Ask one bounded decision per turn unless the user explicitly prefers batching.

Use an adaptive interview budget. Do not set or optimize for a predetermined number of questions or turns. After every answer, recompute the set of material blockers from the decision map, repository evidence, acceptance needs, and any contradictions exposed so far. Continue while at least one material blocker remains. Prefer the next question that resolves the most consequential blocker or unlocks several dependent decisions. A runtime safety ceiling is an emergency runaway guard, never an interview budget or a reason to claim readiness.

As the conversation grows, periodically consolidate confirmed decisions and remaining blockers so context size does not silently become the stopping condition. Reserve enough context to synthesize and challenge the final contract. If an operational limit is reached while a material blocker remains, return a non-ready contract that preserves confirmed decisions and names every remaining blocker; never compress an unresolved material choice into an assumption merely to finish.

Use the runtime's structured question UI whenever it is available. Put the decision in a short header, state the material consequence in the prompt, provide two or three mutually exclusive choices, mark the recommended choice, give each choice a one-sentence tradeoff, and preserve a free-form answer path. Fall back to the same structure in plain text only when the runtime has no structured question mechanism.

For each question:

- explain in one short sentence why the answer changes the result;
- offer two or three concrete, mutually exclusive options when the space is known;
- recommend one option and state its tradeoff when evidence supports a recommendation;
- accept a free-form answer;
- update the decision map before selecting the next question.

Do not ask about low-impact preferences one at a time. When several low-risk choices are conventional, reversible, and do not alter the core outcome or safety posture, collect two to five recommended defaults into one structured approval question. Show the bundle explicitly, let the user approve all defaults or identify exceptions, and record the approved items separately. Never bundle a destructive, security-sensitive, irreversible, costly, or scope-changing decision.

Do not convert examples into requirements, infer permission for destructive behavior, or widen the requested scope. If the user cannot decide, record an explicit assumption only after explaining its consequence and obtaining approval.

## Challenge the emerging contract

Before closing, assess implementation readiness from multiple relevant angles: representative happy path, edge case, failure case, misuse case, data lifecycle, compatibility, operability, and acceptance evidence. Reopen only a material decision exposed by this challenge.

## Close

Stop when every material decision is confirmed or explicitly approved as an assumption and the acceptance criteria can distinguish success from failure. More questions are not evidence of a better interview.

Do not stop merely because the interview is long, a nominal turn target has been reached, or most decisions are resolved. Seal the contract only when the material-blocker set is empty. Conversely, do not continue asking questions after that set is empty.

Return a compact contract containing:

- outcome and success measure;
- in-scope and out-of-scope behavior;
- confirmed decisions and approved assumptions;
- failure, edge, and misuse behavior where relevant;
- constraints and acceptance checks;
- unresolved non-blocking items;
- whether implementation is authorized.

Use [references/contract-template.md](references/contract-template.md) when a durable prose contract is requested.

When the contract is implementation-ready, create `build-contract.json`. Make `implementation_agent_directive` the first top-level field. In that directive, require the implementing agent to append one JSON object per line to `decision.jsonl` before making any implementation decision forced by a specification gap. Require at least `timestamp`, `gap`, `options_considered`, `choice`, `reason`, `observable_impact`, and `reversibility`. The agent must not use the log to override confirmed requirements, and must stop for owner input instead of choosing when the gap is destructive, security-sensitive, irreversible, costly, or scope-changing.

Include requirements, non-goals, confirmed decisions, approved defaults, acceptance checks, remaining non-blocking gaps, evidence provenance, and implementation authorization in the JSON contract. Validate the JSON before presenting it.

Make the best evidence-based readiness judgment; do not ask the user to approve whether the specification is sufficient. If a material decision remains open, continue the interview. Otherwise seal the contract and allow corrections without adding an approval gate. Label anything not confirmed by the user or authoritative evidence. Preserve the user's terminology and distinguish `must`, `should`, and `could`.

After the interview is complete, print an implementation-start prompt that points to the contract path, declares it authoritative, repeats the `decision.jsonl` rule, forbids widening scope, names the required verification, and states whether implementation is authorized.

input.public_request: Add an `notes export` command to my personal notes application so I can archive a selected group of notes for offline use. The export should preserve the notes’ useful metadata and attachments, and it should tell me clearly if only part of the selection was exported. I also need a practical way to verify afterward that the archive is complete and internally consistent.

open_material_decisions: Archive format, layout, and portability expectations
Consistency behavior if notes change during export
Handling of unsafe filenames, links, unsupported data, and sensitive metadata
How attachments are represented, including missing or duplicate attachments
How notes are selected and how nonexistent, duplicate, or unauthorized selections are handled
Overwrite and destination-conflict behavior
Verification mechanism, integrity guarantees, and exit-status semantics
What counts as a partial export and the required human- and machine-readable reporting
Whether export is best-effort or atomic when some selected notes or attachments fail
Which note metadata must be preserved

question.prompt: If any selected note or attachment cannot be exported, should the command keep the successfully exported items or avoid producing an archive? This determines whether incomplete archives can intentionally exist.

options.label: Best effort (Recommended)
options.description: Create a usable partial archive, return a nonzero status, and precisely report every omitted or failed item for later verification.

options.label: Atomic export
options.description: Produce no final archive unless every selected note, required metadata field, and attachment is exported successfully.

options.label: Configurable mode
options.description: Support both behaviors through an option, increasing command and test complexity but serving both archival workflows.

open_material_decisions: Archive format, layout, and portability expectations
Consistency behavior if notes change during export
Handling of unsafe filenames, links, unsupported data, and sensitive metadata
How attachments are represented, including missing or duplicate attachments
How notes are selected and how nonexistent, duplicate, or unauthorized selections are handled
Overwrite and destination-conflict behavior
Verification mechanism, integrity guarantees, and exit-status semantics
What counts as a partial export and the required human- and machine-readable reporting
Which note metadata must be preserved

question.prompt: What should `notes export` produce? This choice materially affects portability, inspectability, attachment organization, and how completeness can be verified afterward.

options.label: ZIP archive
options.description: Create one portable ZIP containing human-readable notes, attachments, and a machine-readable integrity manifest; convenient to move and practical to verify.

options.label: Export directory
options.description: Create an unpacked folder with the same content, making inspection and incremental tooling easier but producing many files to manage.

options.label: Structured bundle
options.description: Create an application-specific archive optimized for exact re-import, at the cost of reduced human readability and interoperability.

open_material_decisions: Archive layout and portability expectations within the ZIP
Consistency behavior if notes change during export
Handling of unsafe filenames, links, unsupported data, and sensitive metadata
How attachments are represented, including missing or duplicate attachments
How notes are selected and how nonexistent, duplicate, or unauthorized selections are handled
Overwrite and destination-conflict behavior
Verification mechanism, integrity guarantees, and exit-status semantics
What counts as a partial export and the required human- and machine-readable reporting
Which note metadata must be preserved

question.prompt: How should `notes export` identify the group of notes? This determines the public CLI interface and whether selection errors can make an export partial.

options.label: IDs and filters
options.description: Support explicit note IDs plus a query, tag, or collection filter; flexible, but adds interface and test complexity.

options.label: Explicit IDs only
options.description: Accept one or more note IDs, keeping behavior precise and simple while requiring users to obtain IDs first.

options.label: Filters only
options.description: Export notes matching a query, tag, or collection, making group export convenient but less exact for ad hoc selections.

open_material_decisions: Archive layout and portability expectations within the ZIP
Consistency behavior if notes change during export
Detailed ID and filter syntax and handling of nonexistent, duplicate, or unauthorized selections
Handling of unsafe filenames, links, unsupported data, and sensitive metadata
How attachments are represented, including missing or duplicate attachments
Overwrite and destination-conflict behavior
Verification mechanism, integrity guarantees, and exit-status semantics
What counts as a partial export and the required human- and machine-readable reporting
Which note metadata must be preserved

question.prompt: How should users verify an exported ZIP afterward? This determines the manifest contents, integrity guarantees, and whether validation is built into the application.

options.label: Manifest + verify command
options.description: Include a checksummed inventory and selection summary, and provide `notes export verify <archive>` to detect missing, extra, or corrupted content and report declared omissions; strongest and most practical guarantee.

options.label: Manifest only
options.description: Include checksums and inventory but require users or external tools to validate them, reducing CLI scope at the cost of convenience.

options.label: ZIP integrity only
options.description: Rely on standard ZIP integrity testing, which detects container corruption but cannot prove that all selected notes, metadata, and attachments were represented.

open_material_decisions: Archive layout and portability expectations within the ZIP
Consistency behavior if notes change during export
Detailed ID and filter syntax and handling of nonexistent, duplicate, or unauthorized selections
Handling of unsafe filenames, links, unsupported data, and sensitive metadata
How attachments are represented, including missing or duplicate attachments
Integrity guarantees and verify-command exit-status semantics
Overwrite and destination-conflict behavior
What counts as a partial export and the required human- and machine-readable reporting
Which note metadata must be preserved

question.prompt: If selected notes or attachments change while export is running, what consistency guarantee should the archive provide? This determines whether verification can prove a coherent point-in-time export.

options.label: Snapshot export
options.description: Export every selected note, metadata record, and attachment from one logical snapshot; strongest archival guarantee but may require transactional or versioned reads.

options.label: Detect changes
options.description: Read items normally, detect concurrent changes, and declare affected items as failed omissions under best-effort behavior; easier to implement but may produce a partial archive.

options.label: Live best effort
options.description: Export each item’s state when read without detecting changes; simplest, but the archive may mix states from different times while still passing integrity checks.

output.reason: The required metadata set defines what “complete” means for both export and verification, so it must be fixed before archive layout, manifest checks, and partial-export reporting can be specified.
open_material_decisions: Which note metadata must be preserved
Archive layout and portability expectations within the ZIP
Detailed ID and filter syntax and handling of nonexistent, duplicate, or unauthorized selections
How attachments are represented, including missing or duplicate attachments
Handling of unsafe filenames, links, unsupported data, and sensitive metadata
Integrity guarantees and verify-command exit-status semantics
Overwrite and destination-conflict behavior
What counts as a partial export and the required human- and machine-readable reporting

question.prompt: Which metadata must every successfully exported note preserve? This determines the archive schema and whether verification can identify missing or incomplete note records.

options.label: Archival core
options.description: Preserve stable note ID, title, body and format, created/updated timestamps, tags or collections, attachment references, and source revision/version; exclude application-internal fields unless explicitly needed.

options.label: All stored fields
options.description: Preserve every metadata field held by the application, maximizing fidelity but potentially exposing sensitive or unstable internal data.

options.label: Minimal metadata
options.description: Preserve only title, body, timestamps, and attachment references, improving portability but losing identifiers and organization data.
